h: מוֹצָאֵי יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, י״ב Motzei Yom Kippur, 12
"For Already": From the Six Days of Creation

p: The heavenly voice that goes forth:
It may be said: what it says, "has accepted," etc.,
implies even the deeds of transgression,
that through their having been forgiven
from the six days of Creation,
'they shall be made white as snow.'"
And when they are made white,
that means that they have become merits.
because in the order of the work of Creation,
Hashem, may He be blessed, created darkness first,
and as they said in the holy Zohar
"There is no light except from within darkness,
and there is no good except from within evil."
And this is what is called "very good"
And this is the wording of the Gemara
that they became like "arranged and continuing," etc.;
And this is the expression "for already":
that is, from the six days of Creation.
through being rectified down to the root,
about which it says, "He shall atone upon you"
and it does not say "for you,"
"For my iniquities have gone over my head," etc.
of having caused damage up to the root,
and the rectification likewise reaches the root.
And this is "Before Hashem you shall be purified"

inlineHeadings.text: Even the deeds of the past

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeishev 11 — “In the future Hashem will clarify, through all Israel doing teshuvah out of love, that intentional sins will become like merits. And this is what they said (Shabbos 89b): ‘If your sins are like these years, which have been arranged and coming from the six days of creation until now.’” Connection: Both tie sins becoming merits to what was arranged from the six days of creation.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Abarbanel, Yeshayahu 1:18 — “Even if their sins be like scarlet — red with the blood of the slain and the oppressed — as soon as they accept the rebuke they will become white as snow and as wool, and no trace will remain, for whiteness indicates purity. We can also explain ‘kashanim’ as actual years (shanim); and so Chazal expounded (Shabbos 89b): Rabbi Yitzchak said, the Holy One said to Israel, ‘If your sins be like these years, which come in order from the six days of Creation…’” Connection: Abarbanel brings the same Gemara on sins that become “ordered like the years,” which Rav Tzadok reads as sins turned into merits.
